Given that price you're probably conflating satellite with cellular/things like 4g. 4g uses cell terrestrial cell towers. Most satellite internet and service uses a relatively small number of geostationary satellites. That's why positioning the receptor just right is so critical. It's also why you might have good throughput (how much stuff comes through per second) but your latency (how long it takes for one new thing to get from server to you) is generally pretty awful. SpaceX will be launching eventually thousands of satellites into low earth orbit, about 1/30th the distance of the geostationary satellites. Receptors will be mobile satellite arrays in a kit about the size of a pizza box.

Ostensibly there would be infinite scalability here without many issues. And the positioning of the satellites means the performance could beat out just about everything not only in bandwidth, but also potentially even latency. Details and specs should be coming fairly soon assuming their early tests are a success. Whatever the case is, it certainly won't be even remotely near anything like $10/GB.
